nail clippers noun

also nail clipper, nail scissors, clippers

classical

Plin. NH 25.58: quod incīsum forficulīs, cribrant (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 164, 374: forficulae, forfex, scissors

forficula, forficulae f.

noun, first declension

small shears; nail scissors or clippers

The diminutive of forfex, the shears that a barber (Mart. 7.95.12) or a vine-dresser (Col. 12.44.4) uses; often plural, like English “scissors”. The nearest classical tool to clippers.

Other words

  • resectōrium, resectōriī n. — nail clippers

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Andresian p. 4

    Not in Lewis & Short: a tool-noun on resecāre, the verb for cutting nails (unguēs resecāre, Val. Max. 3.2.15; Traupman 58). Andresian is our only source for it.

Examples

  • Cedo forficulam; unguēs tibi resecābō.

    Give me the clippers; I’ll cut your nails.composed

See also cut one’s nails, nail clippings, fingernail.
